title: Feelings & opinions
goal: Say how you feel, give your opinion, agree or disagree politely, and link ideas with because, but and so.
intro:
Most feelings in Nepali work like hunger in unit 5: they **strike you** (लाग्नु) or **rise in you** (उठ्नु). 'I'm scared' is **मलाई डर लाग्छ**, 'I got angry' is **मलाई रिस उठ्यो**. And the same verb gives you the most common way to give an opinion: **मलाई लाग्छ…** 'it strikes me…' = 'I think…'.

You'll also learn the connectors that make your sentences flow: किनभने 'because', त्यसैले 'so', तर 'but'.

vocab.note: म खुसी छु / मलाई खुसी लाग्यो.
मलाई दुःख लाग्यो 'I'm sad/sorry (to hear that)'.
मलाई रिस उठ्यो 'I got angry'; रिसाउनु 'to get angry'.
मलाई डर लाग्छ 'I'm afraid'. Of something: X-सँग डर लाग्छ.
म थाकेँ / थाकेको छु 'I'm tired'. Tiredness: थकाइ.
दिक्क लाग्यो 'I'm fed up/bored'. Also बोर लाग्यो.
झर्को लाग्यो 'it got on my nerves'.
चिन्ता लाग्छ 'I'm worried'; चिन्ता नगर्नुहोस् 'don't worry'.
Love for family, friends, partners, places. मलाई तिम्रो माया लाग्छ 'I love you / I'm fond of you'.
मन पर्नु 'like', मन लाग्नु 'feel like', मन दुख्नु 'be hurt'.
रमाइलो भयो 'it was fun'.
अचम्म लाग्यो 'I was surprised'.
लाज लाग्यो 'I'm embarrassed / shy'.
आनन्द आयो 'I really enjoyed it'.
मेरो मनपर्ने खाना 'my favourite food'.
मलाई थाहा छ 'I know'; थाहा छैन 'I don't know'; थाहा भयो 'I found out'.
सोचेर भन्छु 'I'll think and tell you'.
मेरो विचारमा 'in my opinion'.

vocab.en: to accept, agree; to believe in; to obey

vocab.note: म सहमत छु 'I agree'.
Lit. 'if you say why'.
पक्कै पनि! 'of course!'

phrases.en: How did you find it? / What did you think?

phrases.native: मलाई लाग्छ, यो राम्रो विचार हो।
phrases.roman: malāi lāgchha, yo rāmro bichār ho.
phrases.en: I think it's a good idea.
Don't worry, everything will be fine. (तिमी)
You're right. (lit. you said it right)
I'm sorry to hear that. / I'm sad.

grammar.title: Feelings that 'strike' you
grammar.body:
Most emotions use the experiencer pattern: **[person]-लाई + [feeling] + verb**. The verb is usually **लाग्नु** 'strike', sometimes **उठ्नु** 'rise' (anger) or **आउनु** 'come':

मलाई **डर लाग्छ** 'I'm afraid' · **खुसी लाग्यो** 'I'm glad' · **दुःख लाग्यो** 'I'm sad/sorry' · **लाज लाग्यो** 'I'm embarrassed' · **दिक्क लाग्यो** 'I'm fed up' · **अचम्म लाग्यो** 'I'm surprised' · **चिन्ता लाग्छ** 'I'm worried' · **रिस उठ्यो** 'I got angry' · **आनन्द आयो** 'I enjoyed it' · **माया लाग्छ** 'I feel love/pity'.

As in unit 5, use the **past** (लाग्यो) for a feeling that has just arisen ('I'm glad'), the **present** (लाग्छ) for a general feeling ('I'm afraid of dogs').

A few feelings are adjectives with छ instead: **म खुसी छु** 'I'm happy', **म दुःखी छु** 'I'm sad'. And tiredness is a verb: **म थाकेँ** 'I've got tired' = 'I'm tired'.

examples.en: I'm glad to have met you.

grammar.title: Opinions: मलाई लाग्छ… and agreeing
grammar.body:
**मलाई लाग्छ (कि) …** 'I think (that) …' — literally 'it strikes me'. The कि 'that' is optional. To soften: **…जस्तो लाग्छ** 'it seems like …'.

Asking: **तपाईंलाई कस्तो लाग्छ?** 'What do you think?' (about something in general) / **कस्तो लाग्यो?** 'How did you like it?' (about something just experienced).

Other opinion phrases: **मेरो विचारमा** 'in my opinion', **मलाई त्यस्तो लाग्दैन** 'I don't think so'.

Agreeing: हो, **ठीक हो** · **तपाईंले ठीक भन्नुभयो** · **म सहमत छु**.
Disagreeing politely: **त्यस्तो होइन होला** 'it's probably not like that' · **म अलि सहमत छैनँ** · **तर…** 'but…'. Nepalis tend to soften disagreement with होला 'probably' and अलि 'a bit'.

examples.native: यो ठाउँ मलाई सुरक्षित जस्तो लाग्छ।
examples.roman: yo ṭhāuṃ malāi surakchhit jasto lāgchha.
examples.en: This place seems safe to me.
What do you think of Nepali food?
In my opinion, we should go now.

grammar.title: Linking ideas: किनभने, त्यसैले, तर
grammar.body:
• **किनभने** 'because' starts the reason clause: म आउँदिनँ, **किनभने** म बिरामी छु.
• **त्यसैले** 'so, that's why' starts the result: म बिरामी छु, **त्यसैले** आउँदिनँ.
• **तर** 'but', **र** 'and' (between nouns), **अनि** 'and (then)' (between clauses), **कि** 'or' (in questions), **नत्र** 'otherwise'.

In natural speech Nepalis often express 'because' with a verb ending instead: **-एकोले** 'because of having…' — पानी **परेकोले** म आइनँ 'Because it rained, I didn't come'. Recognise it for now; you'll use it more later.

examples.native: म खुसी छु, किनभने आज छुट्टी हो।
examples.roman: ma khusi chhu, kinabhane āja chhuṭṭi ho.
examples.en: I'm happy because today's a holiday.

examples.native: बाटो खराब छ, त्यसैले बस ढिलो आयो।
examples.roman: bāṭo kharāb chha, tyasaile bas ḍhilo āyo.
examples.en: The road is bad, so the bus came late.

examples.native: फिल्म लामो थियो, तर रमाइलो थियो।
examples.roman: philm lāmo thiyo, tara ramāilo thiyo.
examples.en: The film was long, but fun.
Go quickly, otherwise you'll miss the bus.
Because I was tired, I went to bed early.

dialogue.title: After the film
dialogue.setting: Anita and Tom come out of a cinema in Kathmandu after watching a Nepali comedy.

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.en: How did you like the film?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: मलाई त धेरै रमाइलो लाग्यो! तर सबै कुरा बुझिनँ।
lines.roman: malāi ta dherai ramāilo lāgyo! tara sabai kurā bujhinaṃ.
lines.en: I found it really fun! But I didn't understand everything.

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.en: Why? Do they talk too fast?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: हो, अनि गाउँको भाषा पनि थियो। तपाईंलाई नि?
lines.roman: ho, ani gāuṃko bhāsā pani thiyo. tapāiṃlāi ni?
lines.en: Yes, and there was village dialect too. What about you?

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.native: मलाई कथा राम्रो लाग्यो, तर अन्त्य अलि दुःखद थियो।
lines.roman: malāi kathā rāmro lāgyo, tara antya ali dukhad thiyo.
lines.en: I liked the story, but the ending was a bit sad.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: मलाई त्यस्तो लागेन। मलाई लाग्छ, अन्त्य ठीक थियो।
lines.roman: malāi tyasto lāgena. malāi lāgchha, antya ṭhik thiyo.
lines.en: I didn't think so. I think the ending was fine.

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.native: सायद तपाईंले ठीक भन्नुभयो। हिरो चाहिँ कस्तो लाग्यो?
lines.roman: sāyad tapāiṃle ṭhik bhannubhayo. hiro chāhiṃ kasto lāgyo?
lines.en: Maybe you're right. And what did you think of the hero?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: एकदम राम्रो! उसलाई देखेर म धेरै हाँसेँ।
lines.roman: ekdam rāmro! uslāi dekhera ma dherai hāṃseṃ.
lines.en: Really good! I laughed a lot watching him.

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.native: मलाई पनि! अर्को हप्ता अर्को फिल्म हेर्न जाऔँ?
lines.roman: malāi pani! arko haptā arko philm herna jāauṃ?
lines.en: Me too! Shall we go and see another film next week?

culture: Nepali conversation tends to avoid a blunt 'no' or open disagreement, especially with elders and guests. A vague **हेरौँ** 'let's see', **सायद** or **होला** often means 'probably not', and **हुन्छ** can sometimes be a polite way to end the discussion rather than a firm promise. Strong emotions — particularly anger — are kept out of public view; someone who loses their temper loses face. **माया** is a wide, warm word: it covers love for a partner, affection for children, fondness for a place, and pity — मलाई उसको माया लाग्यो can mean 'I felt sorry for him'.

tip.title: Feelings that strike you
tip.body:
- Most feelings use **मलाई** + feeling + **लाग्यो**: मलाई खुसी **लाग्यो** 'I'm glad', मलाई दुःख **लाग्यो** 'I'm sad / sorry to hear it'.
- Some are adjectives with छ: म खुसी **छु**, उहाँ दुःखी **हुनुहुन्छ**.
- Tired is a verb: म **थाकेँ** 'I'm tired' (lit. I got tired).
tip.pattern: मलाई + feeling + लाग्यो  ·  म + खुसी + छु

sentences.en: I'm feeling a bit down today.
Are you feeling down? (to a friend)

sentences.native: तपाईंको कुरा सुनेर मलाई दुःख लाग्यो।
sentences.roman: tapāiṃko kurā sunera malāi dukha lāgyo.
sentences.en: I'm sorry to hear your news.

tip.title: लाग्छ or लाग्यो?
tip.body:
- **लाग्यो** (past) for a feeling that has just come over you: मलाई अचम्म **लाग्यो** 'I'm amazed'.
- **लाग्छ** (present) for how you generally feel: मलाई कुकुरसँग डर **लाग्छ** 'I'm afraid of dogs'.
- Anger **rises**: रिस **उठ्यो** 'I got angry'.
- 'Don't worry': चिन्ता **नगर्नुहोस्** (polite), चिन्ता **नगर** (friend).

sentences.en: This traffic gets on my nerves.

tip.title: कस्तो लाग्यो? — how was it?
tip.body:
- **कस्तो लाग्यो?** asks how someone found something they've just done: खाना कस्तो लाग्यो? 'how was the food?'
- Answer with an adjective + लाग्यो: **रमाइलो लाग्यो** 'it was fun', राम्रो लाग्यो.
- **आनन्द आयो** 'I really enjoyed it' uses आउनु 'come'.
- **मनपर्ने** = favourite: मेरो मनपर्ने खाना.

sentences.en: How did you like yesterday's film?
We had a wonderful time in Pokhara.
I miss my mum. (lit. love for mum strikes me)

sentences.native: म मेरो परिवारलाई धेरै माया गर्छु।
sentences.roman: ma mero pariwārlāi dherai māyā garchhu.
sentences.en: I love my family very much.

lessons.title: What do you think?

tip.title: मलाई लाग्छ — I think
tip.body:
- 'I think…' is **मलाई लाग्छ, …** 'it strikes me, …'.
- Ask **तपाईंलाई कस्तो लाग्छ?** 'what do you think?'
- **मेरो विचारमा** 'in my opinion'. **… जस्तो लाग्छ** 'it seems …'.
- Not sure? **सायद** 'maybe'. Sure? **पक्कै पनि!**

new: मलाई लाग्छ, यो राम्रो विचार हो।

sentences.en: I don't think it'll rain today. (lit. I think it won't rain)

sentences.native: मेरो विचारमा, यो ठाउँ राम्रो छ।
sentences.roman: mero bichārmā, yo ṭhāuṃ rāmro chha.
sentences.en: In my opinion, this place is nice.
I don't think this is good.

sentences.native: तपाईंलाई थाहा छ, बैंक कहाँ छ?
sentences.roman: tapāiṃlāi thāhā chha, baiṅk kahāṃ chha?
sentences.en: Do you know where the bank is?
I'll think about it and let you know, OK?

tip.title: Agreeing politely
tip.body:
- **म सहमत छु** 'I agree'; with someone: तपाईं**सँग** सहमत छु.
- **म सहमत छैनँ** 'I don't agree' — soften it with **अलि** 'a bit'.
- Respectful: उहाँ सहमत **हुनुहुन्छ** / **हुनुहुन्न**.
- **सही** 'right', **गलत** 'wrong'. **मान्नु** 'to accept, agree to'.

sentences.native: माफ गर्नुहोस्, म यसमा सहमत छैनँ।
sentences.roman: māph garnuhos, ma yasmā sahamat chhainaṃ.
sentences.en: Sorry, I don't agree with this.

tip.title: किनभने, त्यसैले, तर
tip.body:
- **किन?** 'why?' → **किनभने** 'because' starts the reason: म आउँदिनँ, **किनभने** म थाकेको छु.
- **त्यसैले** 'so' starts the result: म थाकेको छु, **त्यसैले** आउँदिनँ.
- **तर** 'but' joins two contrasting ideas.
tip.pattern: A, किनभने B  ·  B, त्यसैले A  ·  A, तर B

sentences.native: म आज आउँदिनँ, किनभने म थाकेको छु।
sentences.roman: ma āja āuṃdinaṃ, kinabhane ma thākeko chhu.
sentences.en: I'm not coming today because I'm tired.

sentences.native: म थाकेको छु, त्यसैले आज आउँदिनँ।
sentences.roman: ma thākeko chhu, tyasaile āja āuṃdinaṃ.
sentences.en: I'm tired, so I'm not coming today.

sentences.native: खाना मिठो थियो, तर अलि पिरो थियो।
sentences.roman: khānā miṭho thiyo, tara ali piro thiyo.
sentences.en: The food was tasty, but a bit spicy.

sentences.native: पानी पर्दै छ, त्यसैले छाता लैजानुहोस्।
sentences.roman: pāni pardai chha, tyasaile chhātā laijānuhos.
sentences.en: It's raining, so take an umbrella.

sentences.native: मलाई नेपाली मन पर्छ, किनभने यो राम्रो भाषा हो।
sentences.roman: malāi nepāli man parchha, kinabhane yo rāmro bhāsā ho.
sentences.en: I like Nepali because it's a beautiful language.

sentences.native: म जान्छु, तर अलि ढिलो पुग्छु।
sentences.roman: ma jānchhu, tara ali ḍhilo pugchhu.
sentences.en: I'll go, but I'll get there a bit late.
Why did you get angry? (to a friend)

sentences.native: बाहिर जाडो छ, तर घाम लागेको छ।
sentences.roman: bāhira jāḍo chha, tara ghām lāgeko chha.
sentences.en: It's cold outside, but the sun's out.

sentences.native: मसँग पैसा छैन, त्यसैले हिँडेर जान्छु।
sentences.roman: masaṃga paisā chhaina, tyasaile hiṃḍera jānchhu.
sentences.en: I don't have any money, so I'll walk.
